title: Read a sequence value
summary: A sequence is a separate object that gives out numbers.
introduction: A sequence is a separate object that gives out numbers. Your task: Ask for the next sequence value once more.
learningObjectives: Ask for the next sequence value once more.
Explain the example for read a sequence value

blocks.text: A sequence is a separate object that gives out numbers. NEXTVAL asks for its next value.
Use Oracle Database 19c+ with a SQL editor in a new practice schema. Oracle SQL and PL/SQL do not run in this site's SQLite playground. Create only the named sample objects in that practice schema.

blocks.code:
CREATE SEQUENCE cma_book_numbers START WITH 100 INCREMENT BY 1;
SELECT cma_book_numbers.NEXTVAL AS number_value FROM dual;
blocks.title: Read a sequence value

blocks.text: Read the code step by step

items: `DUAL` lets this Oracle statement return a calculation without an application table.
`SELECT` names the output values. `AS` can give a calculated result a readable column name.

blocks.text: The first NEXTVAL is 100 in this newly created sequence.

blocks.title: A mistake to avoid
blocks.text: Sequence numbers are not gap-free and are not rolled back like ordinary row changes.

blocks.title: Your small task
blocks.text: Ask for the next sequence value once more.
